sections.name: TestTheManifestCanBeWritten
sections.title: Checking that run manifests save and load
sections.what: Checks that a run manifest, the record of which models and prompt versions a run used, can be turned into JSON and read back. It also checks that the model and prompt maps still hold their values in both JSON and Python output, and that those maps cannot be changed after the manifest is created.
sections.why: The comments say saving a manifest failed for every manifest because the map type was not one the serialiser accepted, and no test had called the save step. These tests exist to catch that kind of silent break.
sections.watch_out: JSON output and Python output use different code paths, so keep both checks. A test on only one can pass while the other is broken.

summary: Tests that a run manifest, the record of what a run pinned, can be written and read correctly.
purpose: Checks the serialisation of the run manifest so a provenance record can be explained later.
why: The module docstring says the manifest is the provenance record and that a defect survived because its serialisation was never exercised.
how: Imports the manifest model, the fixture that builds a sample manifest, and the test tools. Only the setup section is visible here, so the test steps are not confirmed.
inputs: A sample manifest from the test fixtures.
outputs: Pass or fail results from pytest. No files are written by the visible code.
risks: The docstring says nothing writes a manifest yet. That claim may be out of date, so check the code before relying on it.
debug: If a manifest test fails, check the fixture builder and the serialised output of the manifest model.
